what_happened: sapience-retrieve.sh: genuine transport failure (curl exit 28): curl: (28) Connection timed out after 3000 milliseconds

Task description (A) offers 'extend an existing cross-language test (LanguageDerivationTest.lean / ValidityLayerTest.lean)' as an alternative to a new NomicLanguage test module. Both are structurally unavailable: ValidityLayerTest pins defeq against the generic PointTruth/TaskFrame validity layer, and NomicValidity is built on NomicFrame D (a different frame type that cannot instantiate PointTruth -- NomicTruth.lean's module docstring records exactly why); LanguageDerivationTest exercises proof systems, and NomicLanguage is a semantic-only component with no proof system. A new module is the only viable route for (A).

Finding (C) is narrower than stated: Tests/BimodalTest/Automation/NormalizationTest.lean already uses 'simp only [formula_unfold]'/'[formula_fold]' (both declared in FormalSystem/Tactic/Attr.lean) at ~14 sites, and LemmaDBTest.lean already reads 'Lean.labelled `tmLemma'. So 3 of Attr.lean's 5 declarations are already exercised; the genuine gaps are truth_norm, reflect_time_norm, and all 5 defs of Tactic/Meta.lean (zero references under Tests/).

Writing the item (C) smoke probe for FormalSystem/Tactic/Meta.lean uncovered a LIVE bug: buildContextExpr's first line is 'mkAppM ``List.nil #[formulaType]', but List.nil takes zero explicit arguments, so mkAppM throws 'too many explicit arguments provided to @List.nil' on EVERY input, empty list included. Measured via lean_run_code: buildContextExpr [] and buildContextExpr [p] both throw. The two consumers (Search.lean:475 tryModalK, Search.lean:527 tryTemporalK) call it OUTSIDE their 'observing?' block, so the exception propagates: 'example : |-[FrameClass.Base] box (p imp p) := by modal_search' fails with that AppBuilder error. Fixing it means editing a FormalSystem declaration, which this task's description puts explicitly out of scope -- flagged as a user_decision on .return-meta.json.

All four recommended artifacts (NomicLanguage test module, ForMathlib smoke module, and the two Automation folds) were compiled green via lean_run_code BEFORE being written into the report, including both host files' exact import closures -- so the plan phase inherits pre-validated content and the implement phase should need no discovery. The compile pass also caught two defects in my own ForMathlib draft (an unnecessarySimpa warning and a 'No goals to be solved') that a prose-only recommendation would have shipped.
